Kyle Anderson (basketball) is an American-Chinese professional basketball player.
Kyle Forman Anderson was born on September 20, 1993.
He is also known as Li Kai'er in Chinese.
Li Kai'er's name is written in simplified Chinese: 李凯尔 and traditional Chinese: 李凱爾.
His pinyin pronunciation is Lǐ Kǎi'ěr.
Anderson played college basketball for the UCLA Bruins.
He was selected in the first round with the 30th overall pick by the San Antonio Spurs in the 2014 NBA draft.
Nicknamed "Slow Mo", Anderson developed point guard skills early.
His height provided him versatility to play as a forward.
As a high school player, he led his teams to two consecutive state titles.
Anderson was named state player of the year during his senior year at high school.
He attended Paterson Catholic High School for two years before moving to St. Anthony High School.
Anderson had his first basketball camp at age three.
His father coached him to be a point guard despite Anderson's height.
Anderson played with older players on AAU teams from an early age.
He began his high school career at Paterson Catholic High School.
At Paterson Catholic, he was often listed as a small forward but considered himself a point guard.
Anderson committed to UCLA in September 2011.
He had also considered Seton Hall, Georgetown, Florida, and St. John's for college.
UCLA coach Ben Howland groomed successful point guards in the NBA.
Anderson and Shabazz Muhammad were top recruits in UCLA's class of 2011-2012.
Anderson finished his freshman season with averages of 9.7 points, 8.6 rebounds, and 3.5 assists.
He struggled at times under Howland's strict offense but led the team in rebounding.
Anderson was named to the All-Pac-12 second team and Pac-12 All-Freshman team.
Projected by NBA executives to be chosen in the first half of the second round, Anderson considered leaving college.
Anderson decided to return to UCLA for his final season in 2013–14.
During the offseason, he worked on improving his midrange and beyond three-point shooting.
New Bruins coach Steve Alford moved Anderson back to point guard.
Anderson had a triple-double with 13 points, 12 rebounds, and 11 assists against Morehead State in 2013–14.
Anderson was named MVP of the Continental Tire Las Vegas Invitational in 2013–14.
He contributed 21 points, 15 rebounds, and five assists to win the 2014 Pac-12 tournament MVP award.
Anderson averaged 14.9 points, 8.7 rebounds, and 6.5 assists per game during his sophomore year.
He was called "the nation's top triple-double threat" by the Orange County Register.
Anderson led the team in both rebounds and assists and was voted the team's MVP.
Nationally, he ranked sixth in assists and first among power conference players.
Anderson was third in the Pac-12 in rebounds and steals per game.
He became the first player to register 200 rebounds and 200 assists in a season.
Anderson's field goal percentage improved by seven percentage points from his freshman year.
His three-point field goal percentage increased from 21% to 48%.
The Associated Press named Anderson third-team All-American.
He was voted to the All-Pac-12 first team and received first team all-district honors.
Anderson was a finalist for the Oscar Robertson Trophy.
On April 16, 2014, Anderson announced he would enter the 2014 NBA draft.
Critics thought his lack of quickness might be an impediment in the NBA.
Anderson was selected by the San Antonio Spurs with the 30th overall pick in the first round of the 2014 NBA draft.
On July 12, 2014, he signed with the Spurs and joined them for the Las Vegas Summer League.
In six summer league games, Anderson spent most time on the wing but rarely as a point guard.
Anderson began the 2014–15 season as the team's lone new player.
He made his NBA debut four games into the season.
Coach Gregg Popovich rested veteran stars Tim Duncan and Manu Ginóbili for the Spurs in the second game of a back-to-back set.
Anderson played 31 minutes in his NBA debut, scoring eight points with eight rebounds, four assists, and two steals.
On December 10, Anderson made his first NBA start against the New York Knicks.
He scored nine points in a 109–95 win over the Knicks.
Anderson received playing time while starting small forward Kawhi Leonard remained out for an extended period due to injury.
During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the Austin Spurs of the NBA Development League.
On February 9, Anderson was named D-League Performer of the Week.
Austin went 2–0 that week, and Anderson logged back-to-back double-doubles.
He averaged 19.0 points, 11.0 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.5 blocks in two games.
Anderson was named NBA Development League Player of the Month for February.
In seven games, he averaged 21.0 points and 6.0 rebounds in 27.3 minutes during the 2015 NBA Summer League.
He became a regular part of San Antonio's rotation in 2015–16, appearing in 78 games while averaging 16 minutes.
On March 28, 2016, Anderson played 36 minutes and recorded 13 points, seven assists, and four steals against the Memphis Grizzlies.
He established career highs in minutes and assists.
Anderson had a career-high 11 rebounds in 20 minutes off the bench against the Golden State Warriors.
In the regular season finale, he had his first double-double with 15 points and 10 rebounds against the Dallas Mavericks.
He matched his career-high in points while adding five steals.
Anderson participated in the Summer League again in 2016.
Spurs summer league coach Becky Hammon declared him the top player in the league.
In three games, he averaged a league-high 23.7 points and six rebounds.
In two games, he followed up with averages of 18.5 points and six rebounds when sent home by the Spurs.
Anderson played 72 games including 14 starts during the 2016–17 season but his overall performance regressed.
The Spurs were eliminated from the playoffs in the Western Conference Finals.
Anderson scored a season-high 20 points against Golden State in Game 4 of the playoffs.
Without any Summer League commitments for the first time as a pro, Anderson wanted to build off his Game 4 performance.
Over the summer, he worked on finishing shots around the rim and getting in shape to play at guard or small forward while also being strong enough to play power forward.
With Leonard out an extended period with a quadriceps injury, Anderson began 2017–18 as a starter.
On November 20, 2017, he had 13 points and a career-high 10 assists against the Atlanta Hawks.
At Oklahoma City on December 3, Anderson started at power forward in place of LaMarcus Aldridge due to an injury.
He was ruled out for two weeks after suffering a grade 1 strain to his left knee MCL.
Through 23 games, Anderson had been averaging career highs of 8.9 points, six rebounds, and three assists.
Popovich expected him to remain in the regular rotation even after Leonard returned.
Anderson returned to action after missing eight games due to injury.
In March 2018, he was moved to power forward as the Spurs went to a smaller lineup with Aldridge at center and Pau Gasol on the bench.
On March 19, Anderson recorded a +30 plus-minus rating in an 89–75 win over the Warriors while being scoreless.

With Leonard missing most of the season, Anderson made 67 starts and ended the season averaging career highs in minutes (26.7 per game), points (7.9), rebounds (5.4), assists (2.7), steals (1.6), blocks (0.8) and field goal percentage (52.7).
After the 2017–18 season, Anderson became a restricted free agent.
He signed a four-year deal with the Grizzlies worth $37.2 million after the Spurs declined to match the offer sheet.
Popovich said the figure was "beyond the pale for us" but he was happy for Anderson.
The Grizzlies' interest in Anderson was strengthened by Memphis assistant coach Chad Forcier, who Popovich credited along with Chip Engelland for developing Anderson.
Grizzlies general manager Chris Wallace called Anderson their "main target" in free agency.
Anderson's role as a point forward increased during his last year with San Antonio.
On November 10, 2018, he had eight points and a career-high 13 rebounds against the Philadelphia 76ers.
He followed up with another game of 13 rebounds against the Utah Jazz.
In his first return to San Antonio on November 21, Anderson had nine points and nine rebounds in a team-high 38 minutes against the Spurs.
In January 2019, he missed two weeks due to an ankle injury.
He returned for two games before being sidelined beginning in February with a nagging shoulder injury.
In April, he underwent thoracic outlet decompression surgery to address his right shoulder soreness and other symptoms.
Anderson said doctors removed his top rib to free the nerve flow from his neck to his right hand.
The operation required him to retrain himself to shoot again.
Anderson was still experiencing discomfort from the shoulder surgery as preseason began in 2019–20, but his recovery went well during the regular season.
Under new Grizzlies head coach Taylor Jenkins's fast-paced system, Anderson played as both a starter and reserve while being used as a small forward, power forward, and center.
In 2020–21, Anderson opened the season with double figures in rebounds in each of the first two games.
On December 26, 2020, he had a career-high 14 rebounds while tying his personal best with 20 points against Atlanta.
He logged consecutive 10+ rebound games for the second time in his career and it was his first game with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds.

In the following game against the Brooklyn Nets, Anderson had career highs of 28 points and four 3-pointers in a 116–111 overtime win after teammate Ja Morant was lost for the game with an ankle injury in the second quarter.
It was the first time Anderson scored at least 20 points in consecutive games.

On May 10, 2021, he logged a career-high four blocks as the team tied a franchise record with 19 blocks in a 115–110 win over the New Orleans Pelicans, which clinched a spot for Memphis in the play-in tournament.
During the season, Anderson made a team-high 69 starts and played mostly at power forward for the first time in his career.
He increased his 3-point shooting after having never made more than 24 in a season and only once shooting above 33.3% in any of his six previous years in the league.
In the Grizzlies' first play-in game, he tied his career high of four blocks in a 100–96 win that eliminated the Spurs.
In their playoff opener at Utah, he set a Memphis franchise single-game playoff record with six steals and added 14 points in a 112–109 win over the top-seeded Jazz.
Anderson moved to the bench the following season after Memphis decided to emphasize Jaren Jackson Jr. coupled with their acquisition of Steven Adams.
On March 3, 2022, Anderson had a career-high six steals against the Boston Celtics.
In the first round of the 2022 playoffs against the Minnesota Timberwolves, he started the second half of Game 2 and entered the starting lineup in Game 3 in place of Adams.
Anderson was the primary defender against Karl-Anthony Towns.
Xavier Tillman became the starter in Game 4.
On July 8, 2022, Anderson signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves.
On December 9, Anderson scored 15 points and recorded a season-high 12 assists during a 118–108 win against the Utah Jazz.

On April 9, 2023, during a win against the New Orleans Pelicans, Anderson was involved in an altercation with his teammate, Rudy Gobert. Gobert struck Anderson after a verbal exchange, resulting in Gobert being escorted off the court and not returning to the game or locker room.
In his first season with the Timberwolves, Anderson averaged 9.4 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game.

On July 6, 2024, Anderson was traded to the Golden State Warriors in a six-team trade also including the Philadelphia 76ers, Dallas Mavericks, Denver Nuggets, and Charlotte Hornets, which became the NBA’s first six-team transaction.
Anderson participated in U16 and U17 training camps for USA Basketball prior to being named to the 2009–10 USA Basketball Men's Developmental National Team.
In 2012, he started at power forward for the USA Basketball Junior National Select Team that competed at the Nike Hoop Summit against a team of international players aged 19 or younger.
In 2023, Anderson said he would consider playing for the Chinese national team.
On July 24, 2023, the Chinese Basketball Association announced that he had obtained Chinese citizenship in advance of the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup.
Anderson is the son of Kyle Sr. and Suzanne Anderson.
His grandfather, Clifton Anderson, played college football at Indiana and had a two-year professional career in the NFL with the Chicago Cardinals in 1952 and the New York Giants in 1953.
Anderson's maternal grandmother grew up in Jamaica; her father was Chinese and married a Jamaican woman, and they lived in Jamaica among the Chinese Jamaicans.
After researching his ancestry, Anderson visited China in 2018 to meet distant family in Shenzhen.
